title: SOPHIE: A Scalable Recurrent Ising Machine Using Optically Addressed Phase Change Memory
problem: Existing Ising machine designs suffer from fundamental scalability limitations where performance drops when problem sizes exceed their physical hardware capacity. This prevents solving large-scale Ising optimization problems prevalent in statistical physics, circuit design, and machine learning.
motivation: Efficiently solving NP-hard Ising optimization problems at scale is critical for applications across statistical physics, circuit design, and machine learning.
method: SOPHIE breaks large Ising problems into smaller independent tiles that work together. Architecturally, it uses multiple stacked chips with optically addressed phase-change memory arrays (OPCM—memory controlled by light) arranged symmetrically to reduce the memory footprint by roughly 50%, and these arrays efficiently perform matrix multiplication. Algorithmically, each tile solves its own piece using symmetric local updates while coordinating through stochastic global synchronization (random-timed coordination), which minimizes wasted computation and communication. Device-level optimizations include bi-directional memory arrays and dual-precision converters.
key_novelty: Breaking large Ising problems into independent tiles with symmetric local updates and stochastic global synchronization (random-timed coordination) allows the machine to solve problems larger than its physical hardware capacity.
contributions: 2.5D chiplet integration architecture combining controller, DRAM, laser sources, and multiple OPCM chiplets for scalable Ising computation
Symmetric local update and stochastic global synchronization algorithms enabling handling of problems larger than physical hardware capacity
Device-level optimizations using bi-directional OPCM arrays and dual-precision ADCs to support the algorithmic approach
Demonstrates 3x speedup vs state-of-the-art photonic Ising machines on small graphs and 125x speedup vs FPGA designs on large problems

metrics.speedup: 3x vs photonic Ising machines (small graphs), 125x vs FPGA designs (large problems)
metrics.area: ~50% reduction in OPCM array area via symmetric tile mapping

limitations: Limitations regarding residual scalability constraints, power consumption, or practical deployment challenges are not discussed.
primary_theme: Scalable optical Ising machines using phase-change memory
